title: From Fire to Writing
question: What came before people wrote anything down?
hook: People farmed for thousands of years before anyone wrote a word.
idea: Farming, domesticated animals and metalworking came well before writing, and writing appeared separately in five places.

beats.prompt: In the Fertile Crescent around 9000 BC, people begin to keep sheep and goats. What else begins at that same time and place?

choices.label: Writing on clay tablets
choices.feedback: This is tempting, but cuneiform spread in the Middle East only by 3400 BC.

choices.label: Wheeled vehicles
choices.feedback: This is tempting, but the pottery wheel was only adapted into wheeled vehicles by 3000 BC.

beats.explain: Sheep and goats were domesticated around 9000 BC in the Fertile Crescent, alongside the first evidence for agriculture.

beats.prompt: Put these in the order they appeared.
items: Sheep and goats are domesticated, alongside agriculture
beats.explain: Sheep and goats came around 9000 BC, the plough by 6000 BC, bronze about 3500 BC, and hieroglyphs by about 3200 BC.

beats.prompt: Match each writing system to where it developed.
beats.explain: Writing developed separately in several places, each with its own system.

beats.prompt: Sort each animal by when it was domesticated.
beats.explain: Sheep and goats were domesticated around 9000 BC and cattle around 7000 BC, while horses, donkeys and camels came by about 4000 BC.
